A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMLU-ProX and support a reliable comparison of text, tables, and figures. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2's Appendices A–G were included. Retained content can be matched despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 25 models with 5-shot prompting and seven with zero-shot prompting across 13 languages in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations across 29 languages, full/lite benchmark results, expert translation ratings, and translation-method comparisons in Tables 3–9.

M1.justification: The Claude 3.7 translation, self-reflection, and external/expert verification approach remains. Section 3.3 changes external verification from GPT-4o reviewing and refining translations to o3 for four African languages and GPT-4.1 elsewhere, flagging discrepancies for human review. This is a limited component revision; expanded stage descriptions alone do not establish an entirely new method.

E1.justification: Evaluated language coverage expands from 13 to 29 while retaining the original languages and reasoning-question domain. Added languages include Wolof, Yoruba, Zulu, Telugu, Nepali, and Ukrainian, substantially broadening the linguistic populations represented in the results.

E2.justification: The evaluated model set adds GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, o4-mini, full DeepSeek-R1/V3, Qwen3 variants, and Gemma3, among others. Gemma2, Llama3.1-405B, and Mistral-7B disappear from the corresponding full 5-shot comparison. The full zero-shot comparator set also changes substantially. Appendix D additionally compares the translation pipeline against reasoning-based translation and native-speaking translators.

E3.justification: v2 adds a separate lite evaluation with 588 test questions and full-versus-lite comparisons, alongside explicit Qwen3 thinking-enabled/disabled configurations. The existing 5-shot and zero-shot framework remains. Section 5.3's sampling description is inconsistent: 20 items from each of 14 disciplines does not yield the stated 658 total items, leaving the precise lite-selection procedure unresolved.

E4.justification: v1 already analyzes model scale, reasoning enhancement, and prompting; v2 revises these analyses for the expanded model set. It also adds full/lite representativeness analysis in Section 5.3 and a direct English-to-Japanese translation-quality comparison in Appendix D, testing aspects of benchmark efficiency and pipeline quality previously unexamined.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or inter-rater agreement. v2 adds mean ratings and accuracy-difference plots but no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 6–9 substantially expand model-language and full/lite result entries, while Tables 4–5 add numerical translation evaluations. Retained entries also change: QwQ-32B's reported English 5-shot accuracy changes from 70.7% to 75.9%, without enough inference detail to establish a same-setting gain. Overall averages across 13 versus 29 languages are not directly comparable.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The added rating rubrics, prompts, and language classifications are empirical documentation rather than new theory.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from an ongoing 13-language benchmark to a 29-language resource with both full and efficient lite versions. The introduction explicitly adds the lite benchmark and broader model evaluation to the contributions. The central claim of persistent multilingual performance disparities remains.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes inconsistent benefits from reasoning enhancement; v2 emphasizes benefits observed for DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3 thinking modes, adds interpretations of language-dependent scaling, and argues that lite evaluation preserves performance patterns. New limitations explicitly acknowledge incomplete expert verification, residual translation errors, and exclusion of multimodal inputs.

D1.justification: v2 adds initial-translation, self-reflection, and editing prompts in Appendix F; detailed scoring rubrics in Appendix E; and annotator qualifications and labor information. It newly discloses vLLM inference and the 70-question validation allocation. Reported total evaluation compute increases from approximately 4,000 to over 10,000 GPU hours, reflecting expanded work rather than a documented per-run budget change.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 substantially revise the benchmark landscape, adding discussions of HLE, MGSM, XCOPA, XGLUE/XTREME-R, and language-specific MMLU benchmarks. v2 strengthens its critique of heterogeneous translation quality and positions MMLU-ProX around parallel reasoning evaluation, supported by a new benchmark-comparison table and positioning figure.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and related work are extensively rewritten, contributions become explicitly enumerated, and results are reorganized into separate Experiments and Analysis sections. A limitations section and Appendices A–G substantially change the narrative organization beyond merely adding experimental content.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one-column to two-column layout. v2 introduces seven figures, including pipeline and performance visualizations, and additional comparison and verification tables. Main results are transposed into a language-grouped table, while expanded detailed results appear in rotated appendix tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens benchmark validation and reproducibility: v1's ongoing verification and preliminary averages gain support from detailed 15-language expert results, a translation-method comparison, explicit rubrics, and reusable prompts. Broader evaluations and full/lite testing further improve usefulness. Reporting defects temper these gains: the lite sampling arithmetic is inconsistent, and Figure 4 gives Telugu's maximum as 71.9% despite a 77.9% entry in Table 3. These defects weaken particular analyses but do not outweigh the substantial improvements in validation evidence and documentation.
